headline: Floods and landslides kill six in Nepal, 407 rescued as rivers breach danger levels
dek: Rain-swollen Narayani, Tinau and Kaligandaki rivers have flooded homes and cut key highways in several provinces, officials say.
body_markdown:
Six people have died and 407 have been rescued since Asoj 8, which fell on September 24, as floods and landslides triggered by days of relentless monsoon rain swept across Nepal, central police spokesperson Avinarayan Kafle said, according to Nepal Press and DC Nepal. Two deaths each were recorded in Bagmati and Lumbini provinces, and one each in Gandaki and Karnali, Kafle said. Two people were injured and are being treated at local hospitals.

The rain has pushed several major rivers past or near their danger marks. The Narayani crossed its danger level at Devghat early Sunday, prompting the Flood Forecasting Section to urge high alert until evening, Nagarik News reported. In Butwal, the Tinau river also crossed the danger level, and floodwaters swept away five houses overnight, Nepal Press reported. In Makwanpur, the Lal Bakaiya river neared its danger level near Jurelibazar, with the same forecasting section again asking residents in flood-prone areas to stay alert, Ratopati reported. Along the Saptakoshi in Barahakshetra, fluctuating water levels have left riverside residents fearful, The Rising Nepal reported.

Saptari district reports the most flooded homes so far. More than 500 homes, 483 in Hanumannagar Kankalini municipality and 17 in Tilathi Koiladi rural municipality, were flooded, affecting more than 2,000 families, OnlineKhabar reported. In Myagdi, a landslide damaged 19 houses and cut power in rural areas as the Myagdi, Rahughat and Kaligandaki rivers rose, OnlineKhabar reported, citing the district administration office. In Nawalpur, the eastern Nawalparasi district, the Kaligandaki river washed away the approach road to a motorable bridge linking the district and Tanahun, severing the Gandaki provincial highway, DC Nepal reported, citing police official Anil Pandit.

## Roads cut in several provinces

The rain has paralyzed road transport in multiple provinces, the Department of Roads told Republica. In Kapilvastu, a landslide near Viral Danda blocked the East-West Highway on Saturday night, Nepal Press reported, citing district police. In Baglung, two national highways and dozens of rural roads were blocked, cutting off the district headquarters, OnlineKhabar reported. Rasuwa's road network remains fully cut after earlier Bhotekoshi flood damage, compounding food and medical supply problems there, Nagarik News reported.

Tourism is feeling it too. A restaurant operator on the Maurice Herzog trail in Myagdi told Ratopati that business has dropped as rain and landslides keep trekkers away.

## More rain forecast, east to improve

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has forecast continued heavy rain through Sunday in Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces, driven by a low pressure system moving in from Uttar Pradesh, DC Nepal reported. Eastern Nepal, including Koshi province, Madhes and Kathmandu Valley, should see significant improvement as the system weakens and exits, OnlineKhabar reported.

In Karnali, Humla district recorded 114.8 millimeters of rain in 24 hours at Simikot between Friday and Saturday, the heaviest rainfall recorded there since 1978, said Dr Indira Kandel, chief of the Meteorological and Climatology Office in Surkhet, according to Nepal Press and Nagarik News. Authorities have not yet said whether the toll or the number of blocked roads will rise as forecasters warn the western half of the country is not yet clear of the system.

nepali.headline: बाढीपहिरोमा ६ जनाको मृत्यु, ४०७ जनाको उद्धार
nepali.dek: अधिकारीहरूका अनुसार वर्षाले उर्लिएका नारायणी, तिनाउ र कालीगण्डकी नदीले विभिन्न प्रदेशमा घर डुबाएका छन् र मुख्य राजमार्ग काटेका छन्।
nepali.take: ६ जनाको मृत्यु र ४०७ जनाको उद्धार अहिलेसम्मको तथ्यांक हो, अनि वर्षा अझै रोकिएको छैन। हुम्लामा सन् १९७८ यताकै सबैभन्दा धेरै वर्षा २४ घण्टामा परेको छ। नारायणी र तिनाउ दुवै नदी खतराको तह नाघिसकेका छन्। मौसमविद्हरूले आइतबारसम्म पश्चिम नेपालमा थप भारी वर्षाको आकलन गरेका छन्। मृतकको संख्या बढ्छ कि बढ्दैन भन्नेबारे अधिकारीहरूले अझै केही भनेका छैनन्। पश्चिमतिर नजर राख्नुहोस्। अघिल्लो बाढीले काटेको रसुवाको सडक अझै जोडिएको छैन।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । लगातारको मनसुनी वर्षाले ल्याएको बाढी र पहिरोमा देशभर ६ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने ४०७ जनाको उद्धार भएको छ। नेपाल प्रेस र डीसी नेपालका अनुसार केन्द्रीय प्रहरी प्रवक्ता अविनारायण काफ्लेले असोज ८ गते अर्थात् सेप्टेम्बर २४ यताको यो तथ्यांक सार्वजनिक गरेका छन्।

बागमती र लुम्बिनी प्रदेशमा दुई दुई जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने गण्डकी र कर्णालीमा एक एक जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ, काफ्लेले बताए। दुई जना घाइते भई स्थानीय अस्पतालमा उपचाररत छन्।

वर्षाले धेरै ठूला नदीलाई खतराको तहनजिक वा त्यसभन्दा माथि पुर्‍याएको छ। नारायणी नदी आइतबार बिहानै देवघाटमा खतराको तह नाघेको छ। बाढी पूर्वानुमान महाशाखाले साँझसम्म उच्च सतर्कता अपनाउन आग्रह गरेको छ, नागरिक न्युजले जनाएको छ। बुटवलमा तिनाउ नदी पनि खतराको तह नाघेको छ। रातभरिकै बाढीले पाँचवटा घर बगाइदिएको छ, नेपाल प्रेसले जनाएको छ। मकवानपुरको जुरेलीबजार क्षेत्रमा लालबकैया नदी खतराको तहनजिक पुगेको छ। सोही महाशाखाले बाढी जोखिम क्षेत्रका बासिन्दालाई फेरि सतर्क रहन आग्रह गरेको रातोपातीले जनाएको छ। बराहक्षेत्रमा सप्तकोशीको पानीको सतह घटबढ भइरहेकाले किनारका बासिन्दा त्रसित रहेको द राइजिङ नेपालले जनाएको छ।

सबैभन्दा बढी घर डुबानमा परेको जिल्ला सप्तरी हो। हनुमाननगर कंकालिनी नगरपालिकामा ४८३ र तिलाठी कोइलाडी गाउँपालिकामा १७ गरी ५०० भन्दा बढी घर डुबेका छन्। २ हजारभन्दा बढी परिवार प्रभावित भएको अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। म्याग्दीमा पहिरोले १९ घरमा क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ। ग्रामीण क्षेत्रमा बिजुली काटिएको छ। म्याग्दी, रहुघाट र कालीगण्डकी नदीको पानी बढेसँगै यस्तो भएको जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयको हवाला दिँदै अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। पूर्वी नवलपरासी अर्थात् नवलपुरमा कालीगण्डकी नदीले जिल्ला र तनहुँ जोड्ने मोटरेबल पुलको पहुँच सडक बगाएको छ। त्यसपछि गण्डकी प्रादेशिक राजमार्ग नै अवरुद्ध भएको प्रहरी अधिकृत अनिल पण्डितको हवाला दिँदै डीसी नेपालले जनाएको छ।

## धेरै प्रदेशमा सडक अवरुद्ध

वर्षाले धेरै प्रदेशमा सडक यातायात नै ठप्प पारेको सडक विभागले रिपब्लिकालाई बताएको छ। कपिलवस्तुमा शनिबार राति विरलडाँडा नजिक पहिरो गएपछि पूर्व-पश्चिम राजमार्ग अवरुद्ध भएको छ। जिल्ला प्रहरीको हवाला दिँदै नेपाल प्रेसले यो जनाएको छ। बागलुङमा दुईवटा राष्ट्रिय राजमार्ग र दर्जनौं ग्रामीण सडक अवरुद्ध भएपछि जिल्ला सदरमुकाम नै काटिएको छ, अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ। रसुवाको सडक सञ्जाल भोटेकोशीमा अघि आएको बाढीको क्षतिपछि अझै पूर्ण रूपमा अवरुद्ध रहेको छ। यसले त्यहाँ खाद्यान्न र औषधि आपूर्तिमा समेत समस्या पारेको नागरिक न्युजले जनाएको छ।

पर्यटनमा पनि यसको असर परेको छ। म्याग्दीको मोरिस हर्जोग पदमार्गका एक रेस्टुरेन्ट सञ्चालकले वर्षा र पहिरोले पदयात्री घटाउँदा व्यापार खस्किएको रातोपातीलाई बताएका छन्।

## थप वर्षाको पूर्वानुमान, पूर्वमा सुधार

जल तथा मौसम विज्ञान विभागले आइतबारसम्म गण्डकी, लुम्बिनी, कर्णाली र सुदूरपश्चिममा भारी वर्षा जारी रहने पूर्वानुमान गरेको छ। उत्तरप्रदेशतिरबाट आएको न्यून चापको प्रणालीले यस्तो अवस्था सिर्जना गरेको डीसी नेपालले जनाएको छ। यो प्रणाली कमजोर हुँदै बाहिरिएसँगै कोशी प्रदेश, मधेश र काठमाडौं उपत्यकासहित पूर्वी नेपालमा भने उल्लेख्य सुधार आउने अनलाइनखबरले जनाएको छ।

कर्णालीको हुम्लामा शुक्रबार र शनिबारको बीचमा सिमिकोटमा २४ घण्टामा ११४.८ मिलिमिटर वर्षा रेकर्ड भएको छ। नेपाल प्रेस र नागरिक न्युजका अनुसार सुर्खेतस्थित मौसम तथा जलवायु विज्ञान कार्यालयकी प्रमुख डा. इन्दिरा कँडेलले यो सन् १९७८ यताकै सिमिकोटको सबैभन्दा धेरै वर्षा भएको बताएकी छन्। मौसमविद्हरूले पश्चिम नेपाल अझै न्यून चापको प्रभावमुक्त नभएको चेतावनी दिएका छन्। मृतक वा अवरुद्ध सडकको संख्या बढ्छ कि बढ्दैन भन्नेबारे अधिकारीहरूले अहिलेसम्म केही भनेका छैनन्।
nepali.social_hook: नेपालका नदी उर्लंदा ६ जनाको मृत्यु, ४०७ जनाको उद्धार, वर्षा अझै जारी।

caption.hook: नारायणी र तिनाउ खतराको तह नाघे, बुटवलमा रातभरमै पाँच घर बगे, पश्चिममा वर्षा अझै रोकिएको छैन।
caption.body:
नेपालमा असोज ८ देखि लगातार परेको मनसुन वर्षाले ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ। प्रहरीका अनुसार ६ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ भने ४०७ जनाको उद्धार भएको छ।

नारायणी र तिनाउ नदीले खतराको तह नाघिसकेका छन्। बुटवलमा रातभरिकै बाढीले पाँचवटा घर बगायो। सप्तरीमा मात्रै ५०० भन्दा बढी घर डुबेका छन्। २ हजारभन्दा बढी परिवार प्रभावित भएका छन्।

म्याग्दीमा पहिरोले १९ घरमा क्षति पुर्‍याएको छ। नवलपुरमा कालीगण्डकीले पुलको पहुँच सडक बगाउँदा गण्डकी प्रादेशिक राजमार्ग अवरुद्ध भएको छ। कपिलवस्तुमा शनिबार राति पहिरोले पूर्व–पश्चिम राजमार्ग अवरुद्ध भएको थियो। बागलुङमा दुईवटा राष्ट्रिय राजमार्ग अवरुद्ध हुँदा सदरमुकाम नै काटिएको छ। भोटेकोशीको अघिल्लो बाढीले काटेको रसुवाको सडक अझै खुलेको छैन।

हुम्लामा सन् १९७८ यताकै सबैभन्दा धेरै वर्षा २४ घण्टामा परेको छ। मौसमविद्हरूले पश्चिम नेपालमा आइतबारसम्म थप वर्षाको चेतावनी दिएका छन्।
caption.trigger: भोटेकोशीको अघिल्लो बाढीले काटेको रसुवाको सडक अझै जोडिएको छैन, यसको जिम्मा कसको हो?

nepali.notes: सम्पादकका सबै दस फिक्स लागू गरिएको छ। मुख्य विवरणमा प्रहरीलाई उद्धारको कर्ता नबनाइएको, कपिलवस्तु र बागलुङका सडकको स्थिति भूतकालमा राखिएको, र अनुवादको गन्ध हटाइएको छ। रेकर्डको कुनै तथ्य, संख्या वा स्रोत हटाइएको छैन।
nepali.editor: The lede and the caption hand police the rescues and state the Kapilvastu blockage as current, both stronger than the record. The caption hook duplicates the card, and several English causative and relative constructions need rewriting in Nepali.

ranking.reason: A live nationwide disaster with a named official toll. Police spokesperson Avinarayan Kafle gives six dead and 407 rescued since Asoj 8, echoed by Nepal Press, DC Nepal and Radio Nepal. River, highway and forecast details carry their own sources, so the core numbers rest on an on-record official statement.

Confirmed as ranked. This is a live nationwide safety story with an on-record toll from police spokesperson Avinarayan Kafle: six dead and 407 rescued since Asoj 8. Rivers, highways, Humla's 46-year rainfall record and the forecast each carry their own named source.

findings.passage: More than 500 homes, 483 in Hanumannagar Kankalini municipality and 17 in Tilathi Koiladi rural municipality, were flooded, affecting close to 2,000 people, OnlineKhabar reported.
findings.problem: OnlineKhabar's Nepali report says more than 2,000 'families' (परिवार) were affected, not 2,000 people. Households in Nepal average 4 to 5 members, so converting families to people without adjustment likely understates the real number of people affected by several times.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'affecting more than 2,000 families, OnlineKhabar reported' or state the actual estimated number of people if the outlet or district office has provided one, rather than silently converting families to people.

findings.passage: This matters beyond the immediate damage. The blocked highways include arteries diaspora families use to reach home districts during the Dashain travel season, and trekking routes into Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, where operators have already reported clients turning back, Ratopati reported.
findings.problem: No source in the article's list mentions Dashain travel season or diaspora families using these specific highways. The Ratopati piece cited (595149) is about one restaurant operator on the Maurice Herzog trail near Myagdi losing business, not about Dashain travel or diaspora road use. Attributing the whole sentence, including the invented Dashain/diaspora framing, to 'Ratopati reported' misrepresents the source and adds an unverified claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Dashain/diaspora claim unless a named source states it, or attribute it to your own analysis clearly, not to Ratopati. Keep only the trekking operator impact, sourced correctly.

findings.passage: Humla district recorded its heaviest 24 hour rainfall in 46 years, 114.8 millimeters at Simikot between Friday and Saturday, matching levels last measured in 1978, said Dr Indira Kandel
findings.problem: The Nepal Press source quotes the meteorological office saying this is the biggest rainfall 'since 1978' (सन् १९७८ पछिको ठूलो वर्षा), meaning nothing that heavy has been recorded since then, not that the level 'matched' 1978 rainfall exactly. The article also blends this with a separate Nagarik News headline citing '46 years', which is arithmetically inconsistent with 2026 minus 1978 (48 years). The two figures are not reconciled.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'the heaviest rainfall since 1978, Dr Indira Kandel said' and drop the '46 years' framing, or clarify the discrepancy between the two source figures instead of merging them into one incorrect claim.

findings.passage: Rain-swollen Narayani, Tinau and Kaligandaki rivers have flooded homes and cut key highways nationwide, police say.
findings.problem: Police spokesperson Kafle is the source only for the death toll, injury count and rescue figure. River danger levels came from the Flood Forecasting Section and highway closures came from the Department of Roads and district police offices, not the central police spokesperson quoted in the body. Attributing the entire dek to 'police say' overstates a single source's authority over facts drawn from several different agencies.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the dek attribution to something like 'officials say' or drop the blanket attribution, since the body already attributes each fact to its specific source.

findings.problem: House style bans parentheses inside sentences ('No parentheses. Use a new sentence'). This also appears nowhere else is checked for consistency, but the rule is violated here.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'since Asoj 8, which fell on September 24' or similar, without parentheses.

findings.passage: Nepal Press reported. In Nawalparasi, the Kaligandaki river washed away the approach road to a motorable bridge linking Nawalparasi and Tanahun
findings.problem: The current official district name used in the DC Nepal source is 'Nawalpur (Nawalparasi Bardaghat-Susta East)', while a separate, differently bordered district still carries the name 'Nawalparasi' after the 2017 split. Using the bare, ambiguous 'Nawalparasi' risks conflating two different districts for readers familiar with the administrative renaming.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the more precise 'Nawalparasi (Bardaghat-Susta East)' or 'Nawalpur' on first reference, matching the source's own naming.

findings.passage: Illustration: AI generated with gpt-image-1. Made for Nepal Wire. Not a photograph.
findings.problem: Running an AI-generated illustration on a story about six confirmed deaths and mass displacement, when multiple wire and local outlets (Republica, Rising Nepal, Ekantipur, Nagarik) almost certainly have real, licensable photos of the actual flooding, risks readers feeling misled about what really happened, even with the disclosure. It weakens the story's credibility on a fatality story.
findings.suggested_fix: Source a real, credited photograph from one of the reporting outlets or wire services for a story involving deaths, and reserve AI illustrations for lower-stakes explainer pieces.

findings.passage: Along the Saptakoshi in Barahakshetra, fluctuating water levels have left riverside residents fearful, The Rising Nepal reported.
findings.problem: This detail is soft color (fear, not a concrete new development) inserted into a paragraph otherwise packed with hard river-crossing facts. It adds word count without adding a verifiable, actionable fact, slightly diluting the news density expected in a tightly packed disaster roundup.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a concrete data point from the Rising Nepal piece (a specific water level reading) or trim the sentence to keep the paragraph focused on measurable river data.

findings.problem: The reporting shows disruption concentrated in Gandaki, Lumbini, Karnali, Bagmati and parts of Sudurpaschim, with the article's own final paragraph noting eastern Nepal (Koshi, Madhes, Kathmandu Valley) is improving. Calling the highway cuts 'nationwide' in the dek slightly overstates the geographic scope for a hook, when 'across five provinces' would be just as punchy and fully defensible.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'nationwide' with a more precise phrase like 'across western and central Nepal' to match the body's own geography.

red_team.summary: The article is well sourced overall, with the death toll, rescue count and most river and highway facts traceable to named outlets and officials, but it contains one clear fabrication (the Dashain travel season and diaspora highway framing attributed to a source that never says this) and one significant number distortion (families reported as people in the Saptari flooding, which likely understates the true human toll by several times). It also blends two inconsistent rainfall-record figures from different outlets without flagging the discrepancy, and misattributes the dek's broad claims to 'police' when the underlying facts come from several different agencies. These are fixable with tighter sourcing discipline rather than a rewrite, and the story itself is timely and relevant to readers in Nepal and the diaspora given the death toll, blocked highways and forecast of more rain.'

responses.response: The red team is right that OnlineKhabar's Nepali report uses 'parivar' (family/household), not individual people, and converting households to a headcount without a multiplier is an invented number we cannot support. We should report what the source actually said.
responses.proposed_edit: More than 500 homes, 483 in Hanumannagar Kankalini municipality and 17 in Tilathi Koiladi rural municipality, were flooded, affecting more than 2,000 families, OnlineKhabar reported.

responses.response: The cited Ratopati story is about one trekking operator's business losses near Myagdi, not about Dashain travel patterns or diaspora highway use. Attributing that broader framing to Ratopati misrepresents the source and adds a claim no source makes.
responses.proposed_edit: This matters beyond the immediate damage. The blocked highways include trekking routes into Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, where operators have already reported clients turning back, Ratopati reported.

responses.response: The source language describes this as the heaviest rainfall since 1978, not a level that 'matched' 1978 conditions, and blending that with a separately sourced '46 years' figure creates an arithmetic inconsistency (2026 minus 1978 is 48 years) that we did not reconcile before publishing.

responses.response: Kafle is on record only for the death toll, injuries and rescue count. River levels and highway closures in the body are attributed to the Flood Forecasting Section, Department of Roads and district police offices. responses.response: House style bans parentheses inside sentences with no exception carved out for date conversions. We should have caught this before publishing.

responses.response: Since the 2017 district restructuring created a separate Nawalpur district alongside a smaller Nawalparasi, using the bare name risks readers confusing the two. Matching the source's own precise naming avoids that ambiguity for a low cost in words.

responses.response: The image caption is fully transparent that this is an AI illustration and explicitly states it is not a photograph, so no reader is misled about what actually happened. We do not hold verified licensing rights to photos from Republica, Rising Nepal or other outlets, and using their images without permission would be a bigger credibility and legal risk than a disclosed illustration. The story's credibility rests on the sourced text, not the image.

The Saptakoshi detail is attributed to a named outlet and reports a real, current condition, fluctuating water levels causing fear among riverside residents, which is standard, relevant color in a flood roundup showing the human stakes along a major river. It is one sentence and does not dilute the surrounding hard facts on Narayani, Tinau and Lal Bakaiya, which remain intact and specific.

The body itself notes eastern Nepal, including Koshi, Madhes and Kathmandu Valley, is improving, which contradicts a 'nationwide' framing in the dek. A precise phrase is just as strong a hook and matches the geography the body actually documents.
responses.proposed_edit: Rain-swollen Narayani, Tinau and Kaligandaki rivers have flooded homes and cut key highways across western and central Nepal, officials say.

defense.summary: Six of nine findings are accepted, mostly turning on attribution precision: converting families to people without basis, misattributing an invented Dashain and diaspora claim to a source that never made it, conflating two different rainfall benchmarks into one inexact figure, over-attributing the dek to a single police source, a house style parentheses violation, and an ambiguous district name after Nepal's administrative restructuring. Two findings are contested: the AI illustration is clearly disclosed as not a photograph and using unlicensed outlet photos would create a bigger problem than a labeled illustration, and the Saptakoshi color detail is sourced, brief and adds legitimate human stakes without displacing the hard facts around it.

rulings.note: OnlineKhabar reports परिवार, which means families or households. It does not report individual people. The article cannot convert that to a headcount. This is a high severity number error and the defence accepts it.

No listed source mentions Dashain travel or diaspora road use, yet the sentence attributes that framing to Ratopati. By the red team's reading, the Ratopati piece concerns one operator's lost business on the Maurice Herzog trail. The defence's fix still keeps the plural 'operators' and 'clients turning back', so the sentence must be narrowed to what Ratopati actually reports.

The source body says since 1978, which is 48 years from 2026. The '46 years' figure appears only in headlines and cannot be reconciled. 'Matching levels last measured in 1978' also misreads the source. The defence's rewrite is acceptable. The key_facts entry must be updated to match.
Kafle is the source only for the casualty and rescue figures. The river and road facts come from other agencies, so 'police say' over-attributes the dek.
House style bans parentheses. The defence's own f6 edit also introduces parentheses and must not be applied as written.

The bridge links to Tanahun and sits on a Gandaki provincial highway, so this is the eastern Nawalparasi district, also called Nawalpur. The article should use the source's naming, but without the parentheses the defence proposed.

The caption plainly discloses that the image is an AI illustration and not a photograph. The newsroom holds no licence to outlet photos. The disclosed illustration is acceptable, and the alt text describes a generic scene rather than a specific event.
The sentence is sourced, short and legitimate color for a flood roundup. It is not an accuracy or defensibility problem.

'Nationwide' overstates the scope. However, the defence's 'western and central Nepal' is also imprecise. The body reports road cuts in Solukhumbu, which is in Koshi, and home flooding in Saptari, which is in Madhes. A neutral phrase such as 'in several provinces' fits the body.
